project.name: Gregg Family Relocation Scoring Matrix
project.purpose: Structured JSON scoring matrix for evaluating long-term relocation areas against Gregg's family, career, education, AI, robotics, fitness, tax, school, rental, and housing criteria.

user_profile_summary.name: Gregg
user_profile_summary.current_role: AI Marketing Specialist with Product Owner responsibilities at Sherwin-Williams
user_profile_summary.long_term_goal: AI Product Leader and eventual university instructor/professor in applied AI business after DBA and MSAI
interests: high school football as a lifestyle nice-to-have
user_profile_summary.preference_note: Virginia is the least favorite option.

spouse_employment.current_store: Franklin, TN - McEwen Southside (1556 W McEwen Dr)
spouse_employment.note: Spouse employer continuity is a second anchor alongside Gregg's Sherwin-Williams tenure, and it pulls toward the Nashville metro rather than Cleveland. Distances to the current store: Spring Hill ~13 mi / 20 min, Murfreesboro ~31 mi / 40 min, Hendersonville ~45-50 min (Green Hills is its nearer store at 20-25 min).
spouse_employment.corporate_hq: Austin, TX (3800 N Lamar Blvd) - relevant to the Round Rock/Cedar Park option as a store-to-corporate career path rather than continuity
spouse_employment.verify: Kendra Scott's own store directory lists Franklin McEwen Southside as temporarily closed with a reported reopening around Sep 1 2026 - confirm current operating status and whether the role is tied to that specific store

work_arrangement.implication: Gregg's employment is location-independent, so no candidate location requires him to change jobs. Local AI/PM job market is therefore option value - a fallback if he leaves or is laid off, plus in-person networking and future mobility - rather than a daily constraint. This is why the remote_career scenario, not the baseline, is the closer match to his actual situation.
work_arrangement.binding_constraint: The spouse's Kendra Scott store is the only hard geographic tie in the household. Location should be optimised around her store plus family criteria, with Gregg's local job market as option value.
work_arrangement.cleveland_caveat: Solon's ai_tech_pm_market of 7.5 rested partly on internal Sherwin-Williams mobility. Remote work weakens but does not remove that argument: what Cleveland still uniquely offers is in-person HQ presence for advancement into AI product leadership, not job retention.

planning_assumptions.rental_target: Professionally managed 3-bedroom townhome with a $2,600/month primary ceiling and a $2,900/month hard stretch cap (income-based; see rental_budget_config).
planning_assumptions.appreciation_assumption: 2–3% annual appreciation planning assumption based on the user's stated May 2026 consensus framing.
planning_assumptions.football_weighting_note: High school football culture is treated as a nice-to-have, not a hard requirement.

alternates.label: Private school scenario (income-contingent)
alternates.basis: Assumes household income supports private tuition at enrollment. Public school quality zeroed as a direct substitute.

alternates.label: Remote career scenario
alternates.basis: Assumes fully remote work: local AI/tech job-market proximity is down-weighted (25 -> 15) in favor of the home base - maker/robotics and fitness community, rental home quality, and university/teaching proximity.

criteria.label: AI / Tech Product Management Market
criteria.description: Strength of nearby AI, software, SaaS, cloud, data, product management, and executive AI leadership career opportunities.

criteria.label: Elite Public School District Fit
criteria.description: Likelihood of accessing strong public school zones, generally targeting 7/10+ GreatSchools or equivalent quality indicators.

criteria.label: Home Purchase Affordability by 2041
criteria.description: Fit against an estimated $820,000 long-term home budget by 2041, assuming broad 2–3% annual appreciation planning assumptions.

criteria.label: 2028 Rental Feasibility
criteria.description: Likelihood of finding professionally managed 3-bedroom townhome rentals near target schools and lifestyle nodes around or near the ~$2,200/month planning target.

criteria.label: State Income Tax Burden
criteria.description: Lower state income tax burden is better. No-income-tax states receive stronger scores, though property/insurance costs should be reviewed separately.

criteria.label: AACSB University / Future Teaching Proximity
criteria.description: Proximity to AACSB-accredited business schools and universities that may support Gregg's long-term goal of teaching applied AI in business.

criteria.label: Robotics, Fitness, Maker, and Indie Builder Lifestyle
criteria.description: Fit for robotics + AI interests, hardware/maker culture, fitness events such as running festivals and HYROX-style training, and indie builder/community opportunities.

criteria.label: High School Football Culture
criteria.description: Local high school football culture. This is intentionally treated as a nice-to-have lifestyle bonus, not a hard requirement.

2041 budget headroom is thin: ~$550K median projects to ~$800K against an $820K budget, versus ~$200K headroom in Round Rock or Georgetown
3BR rent (~$2,460) clears the $2,600 ceiling today but leaves little margin for 2028 escalation
Prices are currently falling (-4.4% YoY), which helps entry but signals a softer near-term market than the 2.5% appreciation assumption
Round Rock and Cedar Park capture nearly the same job market with materially better schools and budget - Austin proper must justify itself on urban lifestyle, not career access

locations.notes: Rutherford County seat ~35 miles southeast of Nashville, and the strongest Tennessee entry on the two budget phases the model is built around. Median home ~$425-480K (working median ~$450K) projects to roughly $650K by 2041 at 2.5%, leaving ~$170K of headroom under the $820K budget - more room than any other TN entry. The rental phase is the standout: average townhome rent is ~$1,765 with 3BR product ranging $1,255-$2,449 and purpose-built BTR communities (Spring Creek, Trinity Point) offering 3BR/2.5BA, all comfortably inside the $2,600 primary ceiling. Market conditions are buyer-friendly (5.33-month supply, 98.25% of ask, only 12.6% of homes selling above asking). MTSU's Jones College of Business is in town and holds AACSB accreditation in both business AND accounting - a dual credential that is rarer than standard AACSB and the most direct professor-of-practice pathway of any Tennessee entry. Football culture is genuine (Oakland, Riverdale, Blackman; the Blackman-Riverdale 'Backyard Brawl'). The binding constraint is commute: I-24 to downtown Nashville runs 35-40 minutes off-peak but 60-90 minutes in the 7-9am rush, which is why the career score sits at Spring Hill's level rather than Hendersonville's. Spouse-employer note: the Kendra Scott store in Franklin (McEwen Southside), the spouse's current workplace, is ~31 mi / ~40 min away - commutable but roughly double Spring Hill's distance.
risks: COMMUTE IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT - I-24 to the downtown/East Bank cluster runs 35-40 min off-peak but 60-90 min in morning rush, materially worse than Hendersonville's 20-25 min

MAGNET TRAP: the headline schools are lottery/application-gated, not address-gated - Central Magnet (#2 of 384 TN high schools), Discovery (#2 of 1,020 TN elementary) and McFadden (#3) are all Rutherford Choice schools requiring a Dec-Jan application window and cannot be secured by buying a house

DUAL-DISTRICT ZONING: inside Murfreesboro city limits elementary runs through Murfreesboro City Schools (PK-6), outside it runs through Rutherford County Schools - parcel-level verification is required and the two districts are not interchangeable

What separates it is cost: Newport's median sale price is ~$1.1M ($944/sqft, up 35% year over year) and 3BR units rent for $5,406-$7,000/month. That is roughly 2x the $2,900 hard stretch cap on the rental phase and projects past $1.5M by 2041 against an $820K budget. Inventory is also overwhelmingly high-rise condo rather than the professionally managed 3BR townhome the rental phase targets.

Nashville.label: Nashville Metro
budget_fit_order: Spring Hill (Summit / Page Zones, Williamson County)
Nashville.note: Ordered by 2028/2041 budget fit. Franklin is retained as a prestige reference but busts both budgets.

key_learnings.learning: No submarket compensation premium. Compensation is set at metro level, not by suburb; higher incomes in premium suburbs (Franklin/Brentwood, Alpharetta, Frisco) reflect who lives there, not employer pay premiums. Where a metro's tech/product employers concentrate in the urban core, core-adjacent suburbs can outperform premium suburbs on career market at materially lower cost. Apply this test to any entry scored primarily on proximity to a suburban office park.

Low school-zone boundary risk is a scoring asset. Where multiple strong public zones exist (e.g. Hendersonville's three 5-star high schools), address-level zone risk is minimal, unlike single-zone-dependent markets (Georgetown TX Leander/Liberty Hill dependency). A school score backed by multiple strong zones carries less downside variance than an equivalent score in a single-zone market.

The rental phase is 13 years and covers all of K-8, while the purchased home covers only the last ~3 years of high school. School quality therefore matters more for the rental location than the purchase location. Screen any 'cheap rent now, good schools later' plan by asking which phase the child's K-8 actually falls in - and prefer locations strong on BOTH rent and schools, which need no phase split at all.

There are two employer-continuity anchors, not one, and they pull to different metros: Gregg's Sherwin-Williams tenure anchors to Cleveland (HQ), while the spouse's Kendra Scott store anchors to the Nashville metro (Franklin). Austin is the only candidate that serves both careers by upgrade rather than continuity - the strongest AI/product market for Gregg plus Kendra Scott's corporate HQ for the spouse. Any plan should state explicitly which career is being asked to restart.

Gregg works fully remote for Sherwin-Williams, so no location requires him to change jobs and the 25%-weighted ai_tech_pm_market criterion overstates its real constraint. Re-ranking under the remote scenario barely moves the order - the top five are identical - which shows the leading locations win on schools, housing and tax rather than local job market. The practical effect is on framing, not ranking: the spouse's store becomes the household's only hard geographic tie.

phase_plan.basis: Encodes the standing convention that the townhome city and the house city may differ, and that each phase should be optimized independently. Added Aug 2026 after the Four Corners analysis exposed a timing problem the flat ranking cannot express.
phase_plan.core_insight: The rental phase is 13 years, not 3. The child is 0-2 in 2028 and roughly 13-15 in 2041, so the rental window covers ALL of K-8 plus the start of high school, while the purchased home covers only the last ~3 years of high school. School quality therefore governs the RENTAL location more than the purchase location - the reverse of the intuitive reading. A location that is cheap to rent but weak on schools does not become safe just because the purchase is planned elsewhere.

timeline.schooling_covered_by_rental: K-8 and the start of high school

phases.label: Rental A - pre-K
phases.school_zone_relevance: None. Child is pre-kindergarten, so school zone does not bind.
phases.guidance: The only window where a cheap-rent, weak-school location is genuinely safe. Optimize purely for rent, spouse-employer proximity and commute.

phases.label: Rental B - K through 8
phases.school_zone_relevance: MAXIMUM. This window carries the entire K-8 run; the elementary and middle zone here matters more than the zone at purchase.
phases.guidance: Either stay put (if the Rental A location also scores well on schools) or relocate into the purchase-target district early, so the child is settled and the 2041 purchase causes no school change.

phases.label: Purchase
phases.school_zone_relevance: Low and falling. Covers only the last ~3 years of high school before the child leaves.
phases.guidance: Buy inside the district already established in Rental B. Avoid a school-zone change at high-school age, which is the most disruptive possible timing.

rental_a_only.meaning: Cheap to rent, weak on schools. Viable ONLY for the pre-K window; holding through K-8 spends the child's elementary and middle years in a weak zone.

single_location_viable.meaning: Strong on both rent and schools, so no phase split is required - rent and buy in the same place. Note the top of the ranking sits here, which is why the highest-scoring options do not need this strategy at all.

purchase_target.meaning: Excellent schools but expensive to rent long-term. Best entered at or shortly before purchase, or via an early Rental B move, rather than held as a 13-year rental base.

worked_example_four_corners.premise: Rent in Four Corners, buy elsewhere.
worked_example_four_corners.rental_a: Davenport / Four Corners - cheapest sub-cap 3BR inventory in the Florida set and Kendra Scott Disney Springs at ~12-15 mi, the closest of any Florida entry. School zone is irrelevant while the child is pre-K.
worked_example_four_corners.rental_b: Move to Oviedo or Lake Mary (Seminole County) before kindergarten. Seminole is A-rated, #1 in Central Florida and 11th of Florida's 67 districts, versus Orange at #19 and Lake County lower. Costs rental affordability - Oviedo rents 6.0 against Four Corners' 8.5.
worked_example_four_corners.purchase: Buy in Oviedo (rank 12, 79.15; schools 8.5, housing 8.0). Already established, so no school disruption at high-school age, and $820K buys comfortably.

drive_times.four_corners_to_tampa: ~60 mi / 60-75 min - not a commutable second market

worked_example_four_corners.failure_mode: Holding Four Corners for the full 13 years puts the child's entire K-8 run in a 4.0 school zone across four possible county districts. That cost is larger than the purchase-phase choice.

phase_plan.caveat: This block records strategy, not scores. No location's component scores were changed by adding it; it changes how combinations of rental_feasibility_2028 and school_quality should be read across a 13-year window.
